citations.label: Flamerix AI gist, Claude Code agent_summary timer (what the call is for)
citations.excerpt:
The answer only updates the agent's status line in the agents panel; it
never reaches the model or your conversation.

citations.label: Flamerix AI gist, Claude Code agent_summary timer (default on)
citations.excerpt:
There is no setting that turns it off, and since
2.1.232 (August 2026) it has been on by default.

citations.label: Flamerix AI gist, Claude Code agent_summary timer (found in OpenTelemetry)
citations.excerpt:
The anomaly was detected by  DRIM  in Claude Code's OpenTelemetry export:
grouping  claude_code.api_request  events by  query_source  showed  agent_summary  costing  more than the main conversation itself .

citations.label: Hacker News, the gist authors post their weekly measurement (share of spend)
citations.excerpt: agent_summary accounted for: 16.4% of total estimated spend (versus 15.7% for the main conversation), and 19.7% of all API requests with approximately 9,000 input tokens per output token.

citations.label: Flamerix AI gist, Claude Code agent_summary timer (estimate, not invoice)
citations.excerpt:
Spend here means Claude Code's own per-request estimate ( cost_usd ), not an invoice: on a
subscription, what you lose is rate-limit headroom.

citations.label: Flamerix AI gist, Claude Code agent_summary timer (cache hit share)
citations.excerpt:
About 98 % of these calls re-read the
transcript from cache; the ~2 % that hit a cold cache carry over a third of its cost.

citations.label: Flamerix AI gist, Claude Code agent_summary timer (missing from session logs)
citations.excerpt:
These requests are not written to the
session logs on disk

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, opening measurement from captured raw payloads (method)
citations.excerpt: Measured over one 4-hour session (27 subagents, 1,496 requests mapped from raw payloads captured with

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, opening measurement from captured raw payloads (request share)
citations.excerpt: 22.7% of all API requests in the session

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, opening measurement from captured raw payloads (scaling)
citations.excerpt: Cost therefore scales with fan-out and wall-clock duration, not with useful work: a session with three concurrent long-running subagents pays six of these per minute.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, second measurement in the thread on 2.1.276 (cache-read share)
citations.excerpt: That is **26 % of the session's cache-read tokens** for ~20 output tokens per call

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, second measurement in the thread on 2.1.276 (cost per tick)
citations.excerpt: the cost per tick is the agent's current context size: a 380k-context agent pays ~45 M cache-read tokens per hour just for its spinner line.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, macOS report that the fork variable stops summaries
citations.excerpt: `CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0` still stops summaries for us on macOS 2.1.312, unlike #105981 on Linux.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, macOS report (cause unknown)
citations.excerpt: The difference may come from the platform or from server-side flags; we haven't found the cause.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, Linux report that the fork variable does not stop summaries
citations.excerpt: `CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0` does not stop `agent_summary` on 2.1.312.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, Linux report (debug-file counts)
citations.excerpt: stock produced 5 summary calls about 32 s apart, `FORK_SUBAGENT=0` also produced 5, and the Bun preload produced 0. Full numbers are in #105981.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, workflow agents are not summarized
citations.excerpt: Only Agent-tool subagents get the timer. In one of our sessions, 1,802 workflow-agent requests came with no summary timers for those agents.

citations.label: claude-code issue 104358, per-request usage missing from disk (problem)
citations.excerpt: Nothing Claude Code writes to disk lets a tool reconstruct what a session cost.

citations.label: claude-code issue 104358, per-request usage missing from disk (billed side queries)
citations.excerpt: Requests with `querySource` `agent_summary`, `auto_mode` (both classifier stages), `compact`, `away_summary`, `generate_session_title`, `extract_memories`, `prompt_suggestion` and others are billed, but appear neither as `assistant` rows nor as `api-request` rows.

citations.label: Hacker News, reply from a Claude Code team member (fleet share)
citations.excerpt: Last week, across Claude Code users who send us telemetry, agent_summary was about 2% of cost at API list prices and just under 4% of requests. In the terminal, where nearly all of these calls happen, it was about 6% of cost.

citations.label: Hacker News, reply from a Claude Code team member (scope)
citations.excerpt: this only applies to background agents that are actively working. They get a summary call about every 30 seconds

citations.label: Hacker News, reply from a Claude Code team member (fix and cheaper mode)
citations.excerpt: We just rolled out a fix for the most expensive case, summaries that miss the prompt cache

citations.label: Hacker News discussion, a reader test with workflows (lower share)
citations.excerpt: It is just for subagents; workflows do not seem affected.

citations.label: Hacker News discussion, a reader test (upper bound in their sessions)
citations.excerpt: In my Claude Code sessions, it looks more like ~8% at most.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, opening measurement from captured raw payloads (what each call sends)
citations.excerpt: Each call re-sends the subagent's entire conversation history plus the full tool schema, on `claude-opus-5`, every 30 seconds per *active* subagent.

citations.label: Flamerix AI gist, Claude Code agent_summary timer (full transcript to the same model)
citations.excerpt:
Claude Code sends that agent's  entire
transcript  to the agent's own model (usually Opus)

citations.label: Hacker News, reply from a Claude Code team member (cheaper mode in progress)
citations.excerpt: working on a much cheaper mode that sends short notes to a smaller model instead of the full transcript.

citations.label: claude-code issue 104358, per-request usage missing from disk (measured gap)
citations.excerpt: In sub-agent-heavy sessions a transcript-based sum lands **×1.35–2.13 below** Claude Code's own `cost-state`

citations.label: claude-code issue 104358, per-request usage missing from disk (internal accounting)
citations.excerpt: Claude Code's internal accounting is correct: list prices applied to `cost-state`'s own token counts reproduce its `costUSD` exactly.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, opening measurement from captured raw payloads (no transcript)
citations.excerpt: These calls carry `skipTranscript: true`, so they appear in **no** transcript.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, a commenter's 30-day numbers (shares)
citations.excerpt: Our numbers over 30 days (129 sessions with background agents): `agent_summary` was about 14% of requests and about 10% of estimated spend, up to 24% in a 40-agent session.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, a commenter's 30-day numbers (Opus share)
citations.excerpt: Opus subagents accounted for about 90% of it.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, a commenter's 30-day numbers (workflows)
citations.excerpt: Moving big scripted fan-outs into workflows avoids the cost and keeps forks.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, a commenter who read the bundles (interactive-only gate)
citations.excerpt: So the fork switch stops summaries only in an interactive session where nothing has set the flag.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, a commenter who read the bundles (settings entry)
citations.excerpt: A settings entry for the variable, in any scope, is the most likely cause of #105981.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, a commenter's 2.1.314 debug log (skipped ticks)
citations.excerpt: The timer skips ticks while the transcript is static.

citations.label: claude-code issue 86879, a commenter's 2.1.314 debug log (what the cost tracks)
citations.excerpt: So the cost tracks how often the agent's transcript changes, not wall-clock time.

citations.label: Hacker News, reply from a Claude Code team member (role)
citations.excerpt: I work on Claude Code.

citations.label: Hacker News, reply from a Claude Code team member (what the summaries are for)
citations.excerpt: These summaries are used for both you and Claude Code to track what each background agent is working on, without reading transcripts.
